news.title: Fed holds at 3.75–4.00% in a 10–2 vote, Cook and Hammack wanted a hike; CME December hike odds 86%, 10-year yield up to 5.025%
news.read: The statement says 'Inflation remains elevated', two members voted to hike and a December hike is almost fully priced, so funding costs are still rising; yet BTC edged up to $81,000 after the decision, a sign this hawkishness was expected. Versus our data: real yield 2.64% (Oct 27), −26bp over 20 sessions, a tight but not worsening rate backdrop; no effect on the market-stage call, Dec 9 is the next test.

news.title: US spot BTC ETFs took in about $176M on Oct 27, a second day of inflows; IBIT about $150M, FBTC $24.5M, other funds flat
news.read: With Oct 26's $110.3M, two days total about $286M, offsetting over 40% of the $636M Oct 22 outflow; but it sits in two funds and the Coinbase premium is still −0.116%, so US spot demand is not broadly back. We added it as a provisional value since two sources agree; the 7-trading-day total stays on The Block's confirmed +$333M to Oct 26.

news.title: WSJ: the US warned Gulf states of a brief, intense renewal of Iran operations after the midterms; Brent up to $111, WTI briefly $103
news.read: Higher oil pushes inflation and hike pressure up, the same direction as the two Fed dissents; BTC did not react that day. Versus our data: BTC's 30-day correlation with the Nasdaq is 0.61, so a risk-asset pullback on oil and rates would be hard for BTC to dodge; macro backdrop only, no effect on the cycle call.

news.title: Strategy shareholders preliminarily approve daily preferred dividends with 99.3%; STRC yields 12% at $99.72, near par, first record date Nov 1
news.read: Daily dividends aim to make STRC more cash-like and widen its funding base; only with STRC near par can Strategy keep issuing and buying BTC, and last week it bought back STRC instead. We cannot see corporate buying directly, only indirectly via the Coinbase premium (still negative); no effect on the cycle call.

news.title: Datavault AI says it has been unable since June to withdraw the rest of about 1,309 BTC from Biconomy and will restate results; shares fell 49.6% in a day
news.read: Counterparty risk at a small treasury company; the size is small (491 BTC were already sold back) and has no direct effect on BTC supply and demand, but it makes the market warier of the treasury-company model; together with Strategy's STRC buyback last week, corporate demand is cooling. Short-term noise.

news.title: Bitwise lifts its 2036 BTC base case from $1.3M to $1.6M (34.3% a year); bear case $130,686, bull $3.67M
news.read: A ten-year allocation assumption, not a market call; it treats the Oct 2025–Jun 2026 drawdown (about 50–53%) as shallower than the past 77–86%, in line with Tidemark's 'shallower bear in the ETF era' hypothesis, but we rely on the Dec 19 low test. No effect on the cycle call.

news.title: Ahead of the midterms Kalshi gives Democrats 90% for the House and 64% for the Senate; Democratic lawmakers say the Clarity Act would not be a priority
news.read: If the market-structure bill stalls in a new Congress, regulation keeps relying on SEC and CFTC rulemaking; limited effect on BTC supply and demand, mainly industry sentiment. Election week (Nov 3) may bring volatility while our volatility readings sit at a 1-year low; no effect on the cycle call.

news.title: Bank of Canada hikes 25bp to 2.50%, saying inflation is 'higher and more persistent than in the July Report'
news.read: Major central banks are turning to hikes under the oil shock, lifting global funding costs, consistent with US 10-year yields above 5%; a tighter backdrop for BTC with no direct short-term effect.

findings.title: New buyers held cost and are back in profit; $84K long-term supply is the next hurdle
findings.lean_why: The thickest pile of new supply did not capitulate at its cost edge and is back in profit while ETF money returned, so the support layer holds; long-term holders are still distributing overhead, so this is a hold, not a breakout.
findings.what: Question: did the $80–82K new buyers hold, and who sells above? STH-SOPR rose from 0.9997 (Oct 27) to 1.0029 (Oct 28, CheckOnChain); the $81,287 close sits 0.9% below the top of the $80–82K bucket, the thickest short-term holder pile (742.9K BTC, CheckOnChain actual coin age, data date Oct 28); ETFs +$110.3M on Oct 26 (The Block) and provisional +$176M on Oct 27.
findings.why: Participants (CheckOnChain Oct 28): short-term holders 3.637M BTC at an average cost of $75,142, long-term holders 16.465M BTC at $49,528. Cost map: true market mean $79,625 (−2.0%) and short-term cost $75,781 (bitcoin-data Oct 22) below; above, the $84K bucket is the thickest long-term supply over price at 819K BTC, then 395K at $90K and 328K at $104K. Two points in time (estimate, Sep 20 → Oct 27): of the 3.623M BTC short-term supply then, 1.107M moved, 411K aged into long-term and 2.104M stayed put; long-term holders moved 601K; new buying since then that has not moved is 1.446M BTC, concentrated at $80K (650K), $82K (416K) and $84K (269K). Fact (model-free): supply above $88K fell from 4.054M to 3.822M BTC, so 233K BTC really sold. Behavior check: short-term holder realized profit 4,866 BTC vs loss 1,975 BTC (ratio 2.46, Oct 28); losses rose only 41.2% over 7 days and did not turn into capitulation; exchange supply 7-day −0.13% (Oct 27). The contradiction: the long-term holder 30-day net position of −212,480 BTC (Oct 27) is still widening and the Coinbase premium is still −0.116%; the only buyers are two ETFs.
findings.alt: SOPR 1.0029 is only 0.29% above 1 and a single-day reading; the 7-day comparison is distorted by the suspected 209K BTC internal transfer on Oct 22. A large part of the $84K long-term bucket may be one entity's internal transfer on 2025-11-22 (Glassnode noted on Oct 28 that about 4.3% of supply at $84–85K mostly came from that day), not dispersed sellers waiting to break even. Changes are estimates (estimated STH total is −2.4% off actual, 8.7% misplaced); per-UTXO, not entity-adjusted, so not comparable in size with Glassnode.
findings.history: The last three STH-SOPR loss lows (Jul 13 0.9762, Aug 1 0.9936, Aug 14 0.9946) were all near $62K and each was followed by a return above 1; this Oct 27 dip to 0.9997 was shallower than all three and recovered in one day. Only 3 samples, too few; background only.
findings.so: Scenario (conditional, CheckOnChain Oct 28): at a close of $80,000 about 1.71M BTC of short-term supply would be underwater, 2.06M at $78,000 and 2.29M at $76,000; from $76K down to $66K it only rises to 2.46M (thin supply), jumping to 2.89M at $64,000. Logic: new buyers did not capitulate at their cost edge and SOPR recovered, so $80–82K is a support layer; long-term holder distribution and the US spot premium have not turned and the $84K long-term supply has not been absorbed, so a 'breakout' does not hold yet. Market stage and exit framework unchanged.
findings.next: By Nov 6 (covering the monthly expiry, the midterms and payrolls): a close above $86,000 (clearing the $84K bucket and Glassnode's $84–85K resistance band) would mean the overhead supply was absorbed, refuting '$84K is the hurdle'; long-term holder 30-day net selling widening beyond 250K BTC would confirm that long-term holders are supplying the overhead pressure.

findings.title: Volatility and supply are compressed together; a break from the $80K zone can move fast
findings.lean_why: Compression only says a move out of the range may be larger, not which way; there is long-term supply above and thin short-term supply below $76K, so either side can move fast.
findings.what: DVOL 37.26 (Oct 28, 1-year percentile 19.2); RV30 25.21% is at the 3rd percentile of the past six months; supply within ±5% of price ($77,223–85,351) is 15.94% of circulating supply (URPD Oct 27), versus 14.91% 7 days ago.
findings.why: Breakdown: implied (Deribit DVOL) and realized (Kraken daily RV30) volatility, two different sources, are both low, and DVOL is still 12.2 points above same-source RV30, so options are not pricing volatility below what is realized. Cross-check: supply concentration rose 1.03 points in 7 days and the FOMC-day range was only 1.77%; Glassnode noted on Oct 28 that 1-month realized volatility is about 25% and only about 5% of days since 2015 were calmer (different method, direction only). The Oct 30 monthly expiry holds 34.1% of total OI, and released hedges after expiry are a common source of volatility.
findings.alt: Low volatility can persist for a long time (realized volatility reached 18% in summer 2023); our concentration record only starts Oct 1, 27 days, and no threshold is applied. The RV30 percentile covers only six months. DVOL fell only 0.43 in a day, not a sharp drop.
findings.history: The brief has no historical sample for this combination of low DVOL, low RV30 and concentrated supply; our concentration record is only 27 days, too few, background only.
findings.so: What changes is the likely size of the next move, not its direction: if price leaves the $80–86K zone, the side with thin supply can move fast (short-term supply is thin from $76K down to $66K). Market stage, exit framework and other reads unchanged.
findings.next: By Nov 6: DVOL above 42 would mean the compression has ended and volatility is expanding, confirming this read; if price and DVOL both stay put, compression continues and we reassess next issue.

research.summary: New Glassnode Week On-chain (Oct 28): thin demand but light selling around $80K, and $84–85K is a band that has turned price back four times this year, consistent with our read that $80–82K held and $84K is the overhead hurdle.

items.title: The Week On-chain: Quiet Under $85K
items.points: $84–85K has turned price back four times this year (about 4.3% of supply, mostly one entity's internal transfer on 2025-11-22); US spot ETF cost basis $81.5K, true market mean $77.9K, short-term holder cost $75.8K; $78–79K bids about $42M; about 4M BTC of long-term supply has a cost of $85–118K; the $3.7B realized profit on Oct 22 was one entity moving coins internally; entity-adjusted profit taking about $260M a day, half the pace of the September-high week; 1-month realized volatility about 25%. Conclusion: range-bound, thin demand but light selling; a daily close above $85K is the first step.
items.meaning: Same direction as ours: support at $80–82K, long-term supply overhead from $84K, and Oct 22 was an internal transfer (already corrected on our side). Its true market mean $77.9K and STH cost $75.8K use a different method from our bitcoin-data readings of $79,625 / $75,781; we keep our own series, and its entity-adjusted figures are not compared in size with our per-UTXO data.

items.title: BTC Market Pulse: Week 44
items.points: Back near $80K after failing at $85K; futures open interest $37.5B (+2.7%), long funding payments above the range top; spot CVD −$80.5M; weekly ETF net inflow $296.8M but front-loaded; supply in profit 67.3%. Conclusion: weak and defensive, but not structurally broken.
